title: Niche topics people miss
objectives: Explain goal-specific inflation, foreign education currency risk and existing assets.
Say why retirement needs an income phase plan, not just a corpus number.
body_md:
These are the goal-planning details that most often get missed.

| Topic | What it is | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Goal-specific inflation | Education, healthcare and some lifestyle costs often rise faster than general inflation | Using one inflation rate for every goal underestimates the costly ones |
| Foreign education | Costs are in foreign currency | Rupee depreciation adds to the cost; plan for it as an extra assumption |
| Existing assets | EPF, PPF, NPS, FDs, gold, insurance maturities already earmarked | Count them against goals before asking for new SIPs |
| Lump-sum events | Bonuses, inheritances, policy maturities | Assign them to a goal immediately, or they drift into spending |
| Retirement has two phases | Accumulation (saving) and decumulation (drawing income) | The post-retirement plan needs its own mix and an SWP, not just a corpus number |
| Health costs in retirement | Medical expenses rise with age | Separate health cover and a health buffer protect the retirement corpus |
| Goal shortfall vs surplus | A goal can end up ahead of plan | Lock in gains early by moving to debt; redirect future SIPs to lagging goals |
| Joint goals and nominations | Goals for children or spouse | Nominations and, where relevant, a will make sure the money reaches the intended person |
| Tax at the goal date | Redeeming for a goal can trigger capital gains | Plan redemptions across financial years where possible; check with a CA |
| Labelling in reports | Tagging folios or SIPs to goals in the client's statement | Makes yearly reviews and family conversations much easier |
example: Foreign education: a weaker rupee adds to the cost on top of the college's own fee inflation — plan it as an extra assumption.
say: Count existing assets against goals before asking for new SIPs.
Retirement needs an income-phase plan, not just a corpus number.
never: Use one inflation rate for every goal.
Retirement planning ends at the corpus number.

check.q: Markets fell 15%. A client's education goal is 11 years away. Should the plan change?
o: No — review yearly, not on headlines; the plan already expects falls

check.q: Why count EPF, PPF, NPS, FDs and gold before asking for new SIPs?
o: Existing assets already earmarked reduce the new SIP needed
check.why: Count them against goals before asking for new SIPs.

o: Decumulation: drawing income, needing its own mix and an SWP
check.why: Retirement has two phases: accumulation (saving) and decumulation (drawing income).
